sentences.text: Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.901/2021 under Section 406/498A/377/354/354B/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Bindapur, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 13.11.2019 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
No child was born from this wedlock.

However, due to matrimonial discord, the couple started living separately from each other since 05.04.2020 and on the complaint of respondent No.2 aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 also filed complaint cases under Section 12 DV Act and Section 125 Cr P C against the petitioner No.1.
During the pendency of proceedings, the couple settled the matter per settlement agreement dated 03.11.2022 before the Counselling Cell, Dwarka Courts, Delhi.
The parties have also obtained divorce by mutual consent.

Pursuant to settlement, the petitioner No.1 agreed to pay Rs.10.00 Lacs to respondent No.2 towards all her claims of alimony, maintenance - past, present and future, stridhan, and dowry articles etc.
3.

Out of said sum, the petitioner No.1 has already paid Rs.7.00 Lacs to respondent No.2 and for the balance amount, the petitioner No.1 has handed over draft No.163582 dated 16.02.2023 drawn on Canara Bank for Rs.3.00 Lacs in favour of respondent No.2, which has been accepted by her.

sentences.text: The petitioner No.1 also agreed to return the clothes of respondent No.2 left at the matrimonial home, and the petitioner No.1 have taken some clothes before the Investigating Officer for returning to respondent No.2, but the respondent No.2 agitated and did not accept the same.

5. In the circumstances, as agreed between the parties, the clothes be taken by petitioner No.1 to the police station for return to respondent No.2 and an amount of Rs.25,000/- for lost clothes, if any, be paid.
This exercise be completed within a week and preferably on 27.03.2023 at 04.00PM before the Investigating Officer.
The receipt be obtained from respondent No.2 and be placed on record before the learned Trial Court.

6. The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, also state the matter has been settled with the petitioners having left with no claim against them and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

7. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has received the settled amount from the petitioners.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
8. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

Consequently, FIR No.901/2021 under Section 406/498A/377/354/354B/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Bindapur, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed, subject to return of leftover clothes and payment of Rs.25,000/- by petitioner to respondent No.2, as above.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
